title: Pre-registered tests: are some 2026 likely-voter screens and recalled-2024-vote weighting methods too Republican?
registered_by: Claude (Polling Lab v20), for independent review by ChatGPT and Kimi
registered_at_et: 2026-11-02 (before any 2026 results exist; publish this file's SHA-256 before polls close)
hypothesis_source: Mike from PA, Oct 28 2026: pollsters apply likely-voter screens and recalled-2024-vote weighting that make results too Republican
sign_convention: signed error = poll (or average) margin minus certified result margin, challenger (D or I) minus Republican, in points; negative means the poll was too Republican
results_required: certified results for the competitive Senate races in data/results_2026.csv (state,dem_pct,rep_pct,ind_pct,source_url)

bootstrap.resampling_unit: pollster (cluster) for H1 and H2; state for H3 and H4

tests.question: Among Senate surveys that published both likely-voter (LV) and registered-voter (RV) results, was the LV version less accurate and more Republican than the RV version?
tests.data: senate_lv_rv_pairs.csv rows whose state has a certified result
tests.secondary_metric: mean over pairs of error_LV - error_RV
tests.supports_hypothesis_if: primary > 0 with the 90% interval above 0, and secondary < 0
tests.minimum_data: at least 10 pairs from at least 4 states

tests.question: Were Senate polls from pollsters verified to weight on recalled 2024 vote more Republican-skewed than polls from pollsters verified not to?
tests.data: included Senate polls with fieldwork ending on or after 2026-10-01, pollster tags from pollster_methods.csv (verified 'yes' vs verified 'no' only)
tests.primary_metric: pollster-level mean signed error, recall group minus non-recall group (each pollster weighted equally)
tests.secondary_metric: same comparison of mean absolute error
tests.supports_hypothesis_if: primary < 0 with the 90% interval below 0, and the recall group's mean absolute error is larger
tests.minimum_data: at least 3 pollsters in each group

tests.question: Would the simple 30-day average have been more accurate without pollsters verified to weight on recalled 2024 vote?
tests.data: v20 simple averages with and without verified recall-weighting pollsters, competitive states with results
tests.primary_metric: mean absolute error (without) minus mean absolute error (full)
tests.supports_hypothesis_if: primary <= -0.5 points and the full average's mean signed error < 0

tests.question: Across competitive states, were the frozen v19 simple averages too Republican overall?
tests.data: v19 frozen snapshot, raw simple averages
tests.primary_metric: mean signed error across states; count of states with negative error
tests.supports_hypothesis_if: mean signed error < 0 with the 90% state-bootstrap interval below 0
tests.contradicts_hypothesis_if: mean signed error > 0 with the interval above 0
tests.caveat: Direction alone cannot identify the mechanism; H1-H3 address mechanism

not_tested_here: Causation: a pattern by method tag is observational; pollster methods differ in many ways at once
Late events after fieldwork, such as the Nov 1 Michigan endorsement
